subject: Dedicated capacity recap & next steps (Acme Health)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Turner <sara.turner@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 08 Jun 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity recap & next steps (Acme Health)

Hi Sara --

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap of what I heard and proposed next steps so we're aligned: 

Pain points we heard
- Production latency spikes during end-of-month reconciliation batch (~800-1,200 reqs/min) that push response times > 3s for synchronous queries.
- Sensitive PHI inference workload needs tenant isolation and strict data residency controls.
- Current on-call team is wary of noisy autoscaling and needs predictable throughput for SLAs.

Goals / success criteria
- 99th percentile inference latency < 800ms for interactive flows, and bounded batch throughput for overnight jobs.
- Isolation: dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs) with VPC peering and customer-managed KMS.
- SLA: 99.9% uptime for the inference endpoint, with 4-hour incident response for severity 1.

Proposed dedicated capacity config (initial)
- Reserved pool: 4x A100-80GB (or equivalent) nodes, pre-provisioned.
- Instance config: mixed instance group to allow GPU hot-swap and maintenance without downtime.
- Isolation: private network + customer VPC peering, logs forwarded to your Splunk instance (or S3) per retention policy.
- Scaling plan: 2x burstable nodes for peak windows (automated via capacity policy), manual approval for escalations beyond 6 nodes.
- Pricing: attached a preliminary pricing sheet (redwood_dedicated_pricing_acme_v1.pdf) - includes reserved monthly fee + overage per token.

Immediate next steps
1) Can you confirm the target SLA and whether 99.9% is acceptable? (If you need 99.95% we'll need an expanded configuration.)
2) Please share the security questionnaire contact for SOC2 evidence and any internal procurement timelines.
3) If this looks right, I'll loop in our deployment engineer (Vivek) to draft a one-week pilot runbook and a mutually agreeable go-live date.

I'll follow up with a short SOW and capacity worksheet. Happy to jump back on a 30-min sync if you want to run the numbers with your infra team.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment: redwood_dedicated_pricing_acme_v1.pdf

From: Sara Turner <sara.turner@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jamal Price <jamal.price@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 09 Jun 2026 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity recap & next steps (Acme Health)

Marissa --

Thanks for the thorough recap. Quick answers inline: 

- SLA: 99.9% is what our app team prefers for now; we'll escalate to 99.95% only if we see production instability after pilot.
- Security: please send SOC2 and pen-test evidence to our security inbox (security@acmehealth.com). Jamal (cc'd) will own procurement and can share timelines - we typically do a 4-6 week legal/procurement review for reserved contracts.
- Isolation: VPC peering + customer-managed KMS is a hard requirement. Also need to confirm data at rest encryption and audit log retention of 1 year.

A couple clarifying questions: 
1) For the burst nodes, will traffic be routed automatically or do we keep failover to the hosted model? 
2) Can you share a sample playbook for incident response SLAs?

If we're aligned I'll introduce procurement and security in a separate thread. We're aiming for a pilot start in early July.

Best,
Sara
Sara Turner
Director, AI Platforms | Acme Health
sara.turner@acmehealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Turner <sara.turner@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>, Jamal Price <jamal.price@acmehealth.com>, procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity recap & next steps (Acme Health)

Thanks Sara -- great, that gives us the lane. Answers below and next steps: 

- Burst nodes behavior: traffic is routed into the reserved pool first. Burstable nodes in the same dedicated pool will auto-scale based on queue depth and token rate up to the configured cap (we'll set cap at 6 nodes for pilot). If capacity is exhausted we can optionally route to a hosted fallback model (subject to data residency controls) - we'll only enable fallback with your approval.

- Incident playbook: attached sample incident response (one-page) and our SLO/SLA appendix in the SOW link. Highlights: 15-min paging for Sev 1, 4-hour on-call response commitment, post-incident RCA within 5 business days. I've attached the SOW draft and the capacity worksheet (acme_capacity_proposal_2026-06.xlsx).

Pilot plan (proposed)
- Week 0: Security exchange + procurement kickoff (outreach to security@acmehealth.com and procurement).
- Week 1: Provision reserved pool + networking (Vivek will own peering and KMS setup).
- Week 2: Pilot load test with synthetic traffic (we'll run 24-48h stress tests to validate 99th percentile latency).
- Week 3-4: Production cutover window (gradual traffic shift, monitoring, rollback plan).

Can we book a 30-min pilot kickoff for next Wed (2026-06-16) at 10am PT? If Jamal/procurement need a different cadence we can adjust.

I'll put the SOW and incident playbook in the shared Drive and update the HubSpot deal. Links: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/acme_dedicated_sow_v1.docx, https://app.hubspot.com/deals/123456789

Thanks - looping in Vivek to coordinate technical runbook.

--Marissa

Attachment: acme_capacity_proposal_2026-06.xlsx
